sources.excerpt: Wampler Pedals Slostortion Pedal Review: A Deep-Dive Analysis for Tone-Conscious Guitarists | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / guitars guitars Wampler Pedals Slostortion Pedal Review: A Deep-Dive Analysis for Tone-Conscious Guitarists By Marcus Reeve August 24, 2026 Released in 2021, the Wampler Slostortion is a dual-stage analog overdrive/distortion pedal designed to bridge the gap between transparent boost, dynamic mid-forward crunch, and saturated but articulate high-gain tones — all within a single compact enclosure. Unlike many 'multi-mode' pedals that sacrifice character for flexibility, the Slostortion leverages discrete JFET and op-amp stages, hand-selected germanium diodes, and a true-bypass switching system to deliver three distinct voicings: Clean Boost (Bypass + Boost engaged), Vintage Overdrive (Boost + Drive), and Modern Distortion (Drive only, with Gain > 12 o’clock). I’ve tested it rigorously over 14 months across studio sessions, live gigs, and home recording setups using Fender American Professional II Stratocasters (with V-Mod II pickups), Gibson Les Paul Standard ’50s (with Burstbucker 1 & 2), and even a Fender American Ultra Jazz Bass. Measured at 9.2V DC under load (using a Dunlop ECB003 power supply), it draws 28mA — slightly higher than average, but well within spec for most isolated power bricks. This review cuts past marketing fluff and delivers actionable insights on where the Slostortion excels, where it demands careful gain staging, and how it compares head-to-head with industry benchmarks. Design Philosophy and Circuit Architecture Andy Wampler and his engineering team didn’t set out to clone any single classic circuit. Instead, they aimed to solve persistent tone problems: muddiness at high gain, loss of pick attack when stacking, and inconsistent low-end response across volume changes. The Slostortion’s signal path begins with a buffered input stage using a Texas Instruments OPA2134 op-amp — chosen for its low noise (2.5nV/√Hz) and wide bandwidth (8MHz). From there, the signal splits into two parallel paths: one feeds a discrete 2N5457 JFET gain stage (biased at 4.7V DC at the drain), while the other routes through a cascaded clipping section featuring matched germanium diodes (NTE104A spec, Vf = 0.28–0.32V at 1mA) and silicon diodes (1N4148) for asymmetric saturation. This hybrid clipping architecture is critical — it generates even-order harmonics reminiscent of tube amp saturation while retaining tight transient response. The pedal’s three-position toggle switch isn’t just a mode selector; it reconfigures internal feedback loops and impedance loading. In Clean Boost mode, the JFET stage operates linearly (bias adjusted to Enclosure and Physical Build Quality Housed in a rugged 1590BB aluminum chassis measuring 4.75″ × 3.75″ × 1.75″, the Slostortion features CNC-machined steel footswitches (heavy-duty 3PDT with LED indicators), gold-plated PCB edge connectors, and recessed, hex-key-adjustable potentiometers (Bourns 300KΩ audio taper for Drive and Level, 100KΩ linear for Tone). All pots are secured with thread-locking compound to prevent micro-shifts during transport. The enclosure’s powder-coated matte black finish resists scratches and scuffs — I’ve used mine on 67 live dates without visible wear. Input/output jacks are Switchcraft 1/4″ mono, rated for 10,000+ insertions. At 1.12 lbs (508g), it’s heavier than a Boss DS-1 (0.82 lbs), signaling serious component density — not just aesthetics. Tonal Character Across Playing Styles The Slostortion refuses to homogenize your guitar’s voice. With a Stratocaster’s neck pickup and clean Fender Twin Reverb, Clean Boost adds air and dimension without bloating lows — I measured a +2.1dB lift at 2.4kHz and only +0.3dB at 120Hz, preserving articulation for jazz comping. sources.excerpt: Wampler Pedals SLOstortion - American High Gain Distortion User Manual | 2 pages Manuals Directory ManualsDir.com - online owner manuals library Search Directory Brands Wampler Pedals manuals Audio SLOstortion - American High Gain Distortion Manual Wampler Pedals SLOstortion - American High Gain Distortion User Manual Slostortion - american high gain distortion Text mode Original mode Advertising SLOstortion - American High Gain Distortion Taking big sounds and putting them in small boxes is a specialty of Brian's, but trying to recreate the well-loved and unique, responsive, chewy-chunky tone of the Soldano® SLO-100® was a special challenge. Brian has always been impressed by the sounds guitarists using that classic amplifier have been able to get over the years, and some of his favorite rock bands feature sounds provided in whole or part by the SLO-100® drive channel. Getting this one right was a personal goal, paying homage to a sound that redefined American high-gain. The SLOstortion adds some major power to the amp-in-a-box style pedal series and brings with it tones that instantly recall the "guitar gods" of the '80s through to today. On top of that, it's a 2-in-1 pedal, with a separately activated and adjusted clean boost (coming after the distortion side of the pedal) that has a certain special character, great for use with the SLOstortion to crank up the volume with your foot, but well-matched to any other pedals, and of course great to slam your amp with. It's a very strong package, we think you'll love it! To get the most out of your new pedal, you'll want to become very familiar with the controls. The SLOstortion's distortion side has a full complement of controls: 3-band EQ with controls for Treble, Middle and Bass, as well as Gain, a Crunch/Overdrive toggle, and Volume. The Boost side of the pedal has its own control, labeled Boost, and a footswitch that acts separately from the SLOstortion's distortion side. As with all Wampler Pedals products, the SLOstortion includes high-quality true-bypass switching which takes either side completely out of the signal path when bypassed. Experiment and enjoy! Bypass Switches– Two true-bypass footswitches ensures solid, mechanical removal of the circuits when they aren't wanted, meaning you don't lose any tone when the pedal is off. Each side has its own LED, so you'll know when one or the other (or both) are engaged/bypassed. Volume – This control adjusts the output level of the SLOstortion. There's plenty of volume on tap in either Crunch/Overdrive mode, so whether you want to go farther than your input level or just make sure it can do unity volume (the same level of signal going out as you feed it, when active), you're covered. The Gain, 3-band EQ (especially Middle!) knobs, and the mode that its in all have an impact on total output volume level, so you're probably better off waiting to adjust the Volume until you've dialed in the other controls. Re-adjustment might be necessary if you get it to the desired level and still need to tweak the sound. Gain – This control, in conjunction with the Crunch/Overdrive Toggle, lets you dial in anything from a light overdrive that's nearly clean to a fully saturated, heavy distortion, without losing responsiveness to your playing and input. IndyGuitarist Wampler Pedals browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal Wampler Pedals SLOstortion - American High Gain Distortion Published on July 6, 2011 Wampler Pedals distortion pedal preview preview preview preview Information Wampler Pedals (preview) Somewhere between the classic distortion tones and the ultra-modern high gain sound, there was an American amplifier that redefined gain... The Soldano SLO-100. The SLO-stortion - American High Gain Distortion. Two gain stages, three band EQ with an independent boost control. The flick switch will act as a voicing option/gain boost. From crunch to full screaming overdrive... The genius in this pedal is the independent boost circuit. This not a simple volume or gain boost, this is a fully functional signal booster (volume and gain) that works independently from the gain stages... so it works when the pedal is bypassed... This is a completely new circuit and sounds amazing... Not only does it give you that SLO-100 sound, but it's really easy to get that ADA MP-1 tone also... So, this one will be able to take you from George Lynch and Nuno Bettencourt right the way back to a more tone driven, sweet all American stack... It's going to be a killer!
